node_kinds.name: GLH_SSHUser
node_kinds.description: A local Linux user account on a collected host.

node_kinds.name: GLH_SSHComputer
node_kinds.description: A Linux host collected by GoLinHound.

node_kinds.name: GLH_SSHKeyPair
node_kinds.description: An SSH public/private key pair identified by its public-key fingerprint.

node_kinds.name: GLH_SSHCertificate
node_kinds.description: An OpenSSH user certificate, split by authorized principal when required for matching.

relationship_kinds.name: GLH_HasPrivateKey
relationship_kinds.description: The source Linux user can access the private key for the destination SSH key pair. Encrypted keys may require passphrase recovery or capture.

relationship_kinds.name: GLH_CanSSH
relationship_kinds.description: The source SSH key pair is authorized to authenticate as the destination Linux user, subject to SSH server restrictions.

relationship_kinds.name: GLH_ForwardsKey
relationship_kinds.description: The source Linux user has an SSH agent session exposing the destination key pair for authentication while the forwarded socket is usable.

relationship_kinds.name: GLH_HasCertificate
relationship_kinds.description: The source Linux user holds the destination SSH certificate together with its local private key. Use requires a usable private key and a valid certificate.

relationship_kinds.name: GLH_CanCertSSH
relationship_kinds.description: The source SSH certificate matches a trusted CA and an authorized principal for the destination Linux user. Certificate validity and SSH restrictions still apply.

relationship_kinds.name: GLH_CanIssueCertificate
relationship_kinds.description: The source SSH key pair is trusted as a CA for the destination Linux user. Control of its private key enables issuing a certificate for an authorized principal.

relationship_kinds.name: GLH_IsRoot
relationship_kinds.description: The source Linux user has UID 0 on the destination Linux host and controls that host.

relationship_kinds.name: GLH_CanSudo
relationship_kinds.description: The source Linux user has an unrestricted sudo grant to root on the destination Linux host. Password-required grants require the user password.

relationship_kinds.name: GLH_CanImpersonate
relationship_kinds.description: Control of the source Linux host as root enables impersonating the destination local Linux user.

relationship_kinds.name: GLH_SameMachine
relationship_kinds.description: The source and destination represent the same Linux host and Azure VM. Both directions model a control bridge between the host and its Azure representation, assuming host-level control rather than an arbitrary Azure grant.

relationship_kinds.name: GLH_HasKeytab
relationship_kinds.description: The source Linux user owns a keytab containing credentials for the destination Active Directory principal. The credentials must remain accepted by the domain.

relationship_kinds.name: GLH_HasTGT
relationship_kinds.description: The source Linux user owns a credential cache containing a TGT for the destination Active Directory principal. The ticket must still be valid and usable.
